name: Coal India Ltd.
business_summary: World's largest coal producer (~780-800 Mt/yr, ~80% of India's domestic output) through subsidiaries (MCL, SECL, NCL, WCL, BCCL, ECL, CCL, NEC); ~75-80% of volume goes to power utilities under fixed-price fuel supply agreements (FSAs) at government-notified prices, the rest sold in e-auctions at a premium. Revenue Rs 1.69 lakh cr FY26; EBITDA Rs 37k cr. Government owns 61.1%. Pays high dividends (yield 6.75%). Subsidiaries MCL and SECL are heading for IPOs (SEBI cleared MCL on 5 Nov 2026).

exposures.mechanism: Domestic coal price +10% blended (e-auction premium moves immediately; notified FSA price changes are rare and politically constrained). Treat as +10% on e-auction (~12% of volume, ~Rs 22k cr revenue) plus +10% on FSA with probability 1/3: effective ~5% of revenue = Rs 8.4k cr; ~25% leaks to royalty/DMF/NMET => Rs 6.3k cr = +17% EBITDA (Rs 37k cr) x EV/MCap 0.85 x persistence 0.5 => +7.2; haircut for hike-denial and volume loss => +6.0. Q2 e-auction realisations were weak (analysts, 30 Oct).

evidence.note: Q2 FY27: PAT Rs6,547 cr, EBITDA margin 19%; brokerages flag cost pressure, weak e-auction realisation (Moneycontrol, Upstox)

exposures.mechanism: Seaborne thermal +15% (Newcastle ~$96): widens import-parity, lifts e-auction premiums and shifts blending users to domestic coal; imports already fell 111->104 Mt (News On AIR 2 Nov). Premium response elasticity ~0.4 on 12% volume => +0.7% revenue ... ~ +2.3% EBITDA x 0.85 x 0.5 +volume substitution => +1.8. No significant pack link (no coal factor in top-12).

Pack elasticity +1.78 per +10% Brent (t +3.7, beta 0.81) is large relative to fundamentals: direct diesel cost for overburden removal is small (diesel ~4% of costs: +5% => -0.2% EBITDA). Fundamental channel is gas-to-coal switching: expensive LNG/oil shifts power and industry to coal. Shrunk toward arithmetic: +1.0 with low confidence; the empirical figure also captures energy-complex/PSU-dividend sentiment.

Power plants take ~75-80% of CIL despatch (model knowledge). +3pp electricity demand growth => +2.4% coal consumption => ~+20 Mt on ~800 Mt of CIL sales; contribution Rs ~1,200/t => Rs 2.4k cr = +6.5% EBITDA x 0.85 x 0.5 => +2.8. Plant stocks >18 Mt but not yet rebuilt (BusinessLine 16 Oct) so CIL is supply-bound by evacuation, not demand, in the short run.

evidence.note: October coal output +19.3% to 67.2 Mt (Business Standard 1 Nov)

exposures.mechanism: BCCL (Bharat Coking Coal) board approved price hikes for certain coking grades (14 Oct 2026) and washed-coal sales at 5% above import parity (26 Sep). Coking ~6% of volume but ~12% of revenue-equivalent: +15% => +1.8% revenue => +4% EBITDA x 0.85 x persistence 0.25 => +0.8.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27: PAT Rs6,547 cr, EBITDA margin 19%; brokerages flag cost pressure, weak e-auction realisation (Moneycontrol, Upstox)

exposures.mechanism: INR 3% weaker raises import-parity coal in rupees => e-auction premium support, and substitution from imports (~6% of India's supply). Revenue +0.4% => EBITDA +1% x 0.85 x 0.5 => +0.5; plus marginal-exporter flows => +1.2 central with the pack coefficient (+1.80, t +1.3) as support.
Net cash (cash >Rs 1.1 lakh cr incl. FDs, model knowledge): no funding-cost risk; stock is a 6.75% yield bond proxy, ~1.4% value per 25bp on its duration x 0.5 => -0.7.

+1 = higher royalty/cess. Royalty and levies are ~14% ad valorem plus fixed levies; a rise is passed to FSA consumers only with a lag and cap; assume 30% unrecovered of a +1pp rise => ~-1.2% EBITDA ... with probability of larger changes => -2.0.

Employee cost ~25% of operating costs (~Rs 32k cr, model knowledge); +2pp wage growth including NCWA-XI/labour-code provisions => +Rs 640 cr = -1.7% EBITDA x 0.85 x persistence 0.8 => -1.2. Brokerages flagged cost pressure post Q2.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27: PAT Rs6,547 cr, EBITDA margin 19%; brokerages flag cost pressure, weak e-auction realisation (Moneycontrol, Upstox)

exposures.mechanism: Renewable build-out and ethanol/gasification policy displace thermal coal at the margin; but demand growth to 2030 remains positive and CIL is guided to 1 bn t. -1.0 per unit shock reflects terminal-value risk on a 7x P/E stock.
Discom payment reform keeps receivables low (CIL collects in advance for most FSA, model knowledge) and stabilises offtake; small positive.

supply_chain.counterparty: Steel makers (washed coking coal via BCCL/CCL)
